newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian rebels kill nine soldiers, police.
newsitem.headline: Colombian rebels kill nine soldiers, police.

text.p: Leftist guerrillas killed nine security force members and wounded 18 in fighting in central and eastern Colombia over the weekend, police sources and local media reported on Sunday.

Five soldiers were killed and 13 wounded on Sunday during intense clashes with Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels near the town of Uribe in eastern Meta province, the Radionet radio network reported, citing unnamed military sources.
An army spokesman in Bogota confirmed the battles around Uribe but was unable to confirm the death toll.

Three soldiers were killed when a landmine planted by suspected National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrillas exploded under their truck near Saravena in the eastern province of Arauca on Sunday, Radionet said. Army officials were unavailable to confirm details.
In further fighting overnight on Saturday and early on Sunday, FARC insurgents stormed two towns south of Bogota, killing one policeman and wounding five, officials said.
An initial assault, in which one policeman was wounded, took place on Saturday evening in Une, about 15 miles (25 km) outside the capital.

Fighting broke out shortly afterward in the town of Gutierrez, another 10 miles (16 km) south of Une, and lasted until the early hours of Sunday, said Gen. Alfredo Salgado, operational head of the National Police. One policeman died and four were injured in the fighting, he said.

FARC rebels, meanwhile, released two Brazilian highway engineers kidnapped last August, a Red Cross official said. The two men were freed late on Friday near Villavicencio. It was not clear whether a ransom had been paid.
Demetrio Mendoza and Eduardo Babtista had been supervising the building of a new highway between Bogota and Villavicencio, gateway to the eastern plains region.

The FARC is Latin America's oldest and largest guerrilla army. It was set up as a pro-Soviet force in 1964 and partly finances its long-running uprising with the proceeds of kidnappings and extortion.
